precepts.text: Judah mourneth; they are black unto the ground.
precepts.point: The chief captain asked Paul, art not thou that Egyptian? Joseph, Moses and Paul all passed for Egyptians.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.why:
When Paul was led into the castle, the chief captain asked, “Canst thou speak Greek? Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?” He took Paul for a specific Egyptian. “But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus”. Paul passed for an Egyptian. Moses passed for an Egyptian. Joseph passed for an Egyptian. Christ passed too: his family ran into Africa from white folks. What more do you possibly need at this point?

Jeremiah shows what Judah looked like: “Judah mourneth, and the gates thereof languish; they are black unto the ground; and the cry of Jerusalem is gone up.” Jeremiah is speaking of the same situation he wrote of in Lamentations, when Babylon came, overthrew us and starved us. We became blacker to the ground: dark, swelled bellies, ribs showing, ribs touching. That is how we looked when Babylon besieged us for those years.

Some try to say it is only symbolic. No: it is the same thing, and Jeremiah, who wrote Lamentations, is saying the same thing in both places. Calling it symbolic is simple and unfaithful and weak.

So the chief captain looking at a Jew and seeing an Egyptian makes sense. Judah was black, and a Jew of Tarsus could pass for an Egyptian because our people looked like the people of Africa. Israel sits in Western Asia bordering North Africa, one land mass, and all the native inhabitants of that region were nonwhite.

precepts.text: They are black unto the ground: you are dark and black like the dust you were formed from, and like him.
precepts.point: They are trying to break and mar the image he created in you — girls made to cut their hair off at school.

precepts.text: The ground is chapt, for there was no rain; the hind forsook her calf and the wild asses' eyes did fail because there was no grass, for our backslidings are many, we have sinned against thee.
precepts.point: The things written aforetime were written for our learning: Jeremiah shows this curse landing in Israel's history, the ground chapt because there was no rain, and the confession that our backslidings are many.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
Here is the shut heaven landing in Israel's history. “Because the ground is chapt, for there was no rain in the earth, the plowmen were ashamed, they covered their heads.” Exactly what Moses warned: the Lord shut up the heaven, there was no rain, and the land did not yield her fruit; the plowmen had nothing to show.

“Yea, the hind also calved in the field, and forsook it, because there was no grass. And the wild asses did stand in the high places, they snuffed up the wind like dragons; their eyes did fail, because there was no grass.” With no grass the animals have nothing to feed on: the hind forsook her own calf, and the eyes of the wild asses failed. The crops cannot grow, the cattle go lean, and there is no meat to eat.

And the reason is confessed: “O Lord, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy name’s sake: for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against thee.” The heart was deceived, Israel turned aside, and the drought came just as Deuteronomy 11 says. These things were written for our learning.

precepts.text: The Most High does not hear sinners; He told Jeremiah not to pray for them because their sins were, and are, so many, which is why it behooves all of us to repent.
precepts.point: He tells Jeremiah not to pray for this people; even when they fast He will not hear their cry, and their offerings He will not accept, but will consume them by sword, famine and pestilence.

note.label: Jeremiah 14: The Drought and the False Prophets

precepts.why:
The Lord tells Jeremiah, “Pray not for this people for their good”, and says that when they fast he will not hear their cry. John gives the rule behind it: “Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him he heareth.”

The people loved to wander and did not refrain their feet; their sins were so many that he would remember their iniquity and visit their sins. He told Jeremiah not to pray for them because their sins were, and are, so many. God does not hear sinners; he hears the man that worships him and does his will.

That is why it behooves all of us to repent. Fasting and offerings will not be heard from a people that keep wandering; he hears those that do his will.

moments.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: We acknowledge, O Lord, our wickedness and the iniquity of our fathers, for we have sinned against thee. Accountability is what Christianity does not teach; its doctrine is excuses, fall and stay down because Christ died for you. The Bible says you fall and get back up.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Judah mourneth, and the gates thereof languish; they are black unto the ground. A brother sent a long message saying he was leaving the camp because this is only talking about a condition.
All right -- let us roll with their argument and follow it through the prophets.

If you want to leave, tell the truth and be honest. Do not sit up there and say you are leaving because we are teaching the wrong thing. He also said he could not see himself on the street teaching it, and I have never seen him teach.
The word comes concerning the dearth. Judah mourns, the gates languish, and the cry of Jerusalem goes up while the nobles send their little ones for water and find none.

note.label: Jeremiah 14: The Drought and the False Prophets

points: The ground is chapped because there is no rain, and the plowmen are ashamed and cover their heads. That is how you know these are black people; "chapped" is a word black people use, not just for lips but for the cracked, dry ground.

note.label: Jeremiah 14: The Drought and the False Prophets

points: Though our iniquities testify against us, the plea is that the Most High act for His name's sake, for our backslidings are many. He is called the hope of Israel and the Savior in time of trouble.

note.label: Jeremiah 14: The Drought and the False Prophets

points: The cry is for Him not to be a stranger in the land or a mighty man that cannot save, since He is in the midst of us and we are called by His name.

note.label: Jeremiah 14: The Drought and the False Prophets

points: The people loved to wander and did not refrain their feet, so the Most High does not accept them; He will remember their iniquity and visit their sins.

note.label: Jeremiah 14: The Drought and the False Prophets

points: He tells Jeremiah not to pray for this people; even when they fast He will not hear their cry, and their offerings He will not accept, but will consume them by sword, famine and pestilence.

note.label: Jeremiah 14: The Drought and the False Prophets

points: Jeremiah answers that the prophets tell the people they shall not see sword or famine but shall have assured peace. This is what the Christian pastors do today; the verse above said not to pray for these people, yet the false prophets promise nothing but peace and prosperity.

What happened back then is happening today. This country is going to go down by nuclear destruction, whether our people accept it or not, while the false prophets say nothing but peace, and they will be dealt with like all the other nations.

note.label: Jeremiah 14: The Drought and the False Prophets

points: The Most High says those prophets prophesy lies in His name; He did not send them. By sword and famine those prophets shall be consumed, and the people they deceived cast out in the streets with none to bury them.

note.label: Jeremiah 14: The Drought and the False Prophets

points: Let the eyes run down with tears night and day, for the virgin daughter of the people is broken with a great breach; the slain fill the field and the sick with famine fill the city, while prophet and priest wander into a land they know not.

note.label: Jeremiah 14: The Drought and the False Prophets

points: We have to acknowledge our offense and the wickedness we have been doing, even the wickedness we support because it does not affect us directly. Your salvation is contingent on keeping the commandments and abhorring that evil.

note.label: Jeremiah 14: The Drought and the False Prophets

points: We acknowledge our wickedness and the iniquity of our fathers and ask Him not to abhor us for His name's sake or break His covenant. None of the vanities of the gentiles can cause rain; only the Most High, so we wait upon Him.
